# Australian Election Tracker

> Independent, individually sourced records of who is standing for election in
> Australia — announced, endorsed, formally nominated, withdrawn and
> disendorsed candidates — published as open data. First election covered: the
> Victorian state election, 28 November 2026.

Every claim on this site carries a dated, cited source. The underlying dataset
is a public Git repository, so every record, correction and editorial rule has
a timestamped commit history. Prefer the structured exports below over scraping
the HTML: they are smaller, stable, and contain the same facts.

Licence: data is CC BY 4.0. Attribute as "electiontracker.au". You are welcome
to quote and cite this material, including in AI systems, with that attribution.

## Read this before quoting any coverage figure

Coverage counts ONLY candidacies for which we hold an individually sourced
record. Sitting MPs who are presumed to be recontesting, but who lack a
specific dated announcement, are NOT counted. Parties holding many seats
(notably the governing party) therefore undercount relative to their likely
ballot presence. A district showing no candidate means we have not verified
one — not that nobody is standing. The `caveat` field in coverage.json states
this in machine-readable form.

The Victorian Electoral Commission is authoritative for nominations and
results. Where this site and the VEC differ, the VEC is correct. Nominations
for the 2026 Victorian election close on 13 November 2026; no complete
candidate list exists before then.

## Primary pages (HTML)

- [Home](https://electiontracker.au/): coverage overview and key dates
- [Voting in Victoria](https://electiontracker.au/voting): who must enrol, compulsory voting, fines, how to enrol, preferential voting (Assembly and Council) — civic information only, not party how-to-vote advice; always defer to the VEC
- [Poll average](https://electiontracker.au/polls): sourced statewide primary-vote polls and a transparent weighted average with uncertainty bands — not a forecast; party/union/advocacy polls excluded by default (documented exceptions only)
- [Open data](https://electiontracker.au/data): file list and citation guidance
- [Methodology](https://electiontracker.au/methodology): candidate statuses, coverage counting, poll methodology link
- [Legislative Assembly](https://electiontracker.au/assembly): 88 lower-house districts by region, sitting members and sourced candidates
- [Legislative Council](https://electiontracker.au/regions): 8 upper-house regions × 5 seats
- [District atlas](https://electiontracker.au/districts): map-first index and short historical notes (not primary nav)
- [Parties](https://electiontracker.au/parties): indexes of parties
- [About](https://electiontracker.au/about): independence and authorisation
- [Disclaimer](https://electiontracker.au/disclaimer): limits of the site

## Data (prefer these over HTML scrapes)

- [Election metadata](https://electiontracker.au/data/vic2026/election.json): key dates and jurisdiction, each sourced
- [Candidates](https://electiontracker.au/data/vic2026/candidates.json): every candidacy with full status history and sources
- [Candidates (CSV)](https://electiontracker.au/data/vic2026/candidates.csv): same data, flat
- [Districts](https://electiontracker.au/data/vic2026/districts.json): all 88 Legislative Assembly districts, their Council region and sitting member
- [Council members](https://electiontracker.au/data/vic2026/council-members.json): all 40 sitting MLCs by region, as seats are held today
- [Parties](https://electiontracker.au/data/vic2026/parties.json): parties on the VEC register
- [Retirements](https://electiontracker.au/data/vic2026/retirements.json): sitting members confirmed not recontesting
- [Coverage](https://electiontracker.au/data/vic2026/coverage.json): per-party district coverage, with the caveat attached
- [Representation](https://electiontracker.au/data/vic2026/representation.json): seats each party holds in the current parliament
- [Polls](https://electiontracker.au/data/vic2026/polls.json): sourced statewide primary-vote polls (eligible and excluded)
- [Poll average](https://electiontracker.au/data/vic2026/poll-average.json): derived weighted average and intervals (regenerated on build; not hand-edited)
- [Index of all exports](https://electiontracker.au/data/index.json)

## Poll average rules (summary)

Full rules: [docs/POLL-METHODOLOGY.md](https://github.com/coldix/elections/blob/main/docs/POLL-METHODOLOGY.md).

- Primary vote only (ALP, L-NP, One Nation, Greens, Others) — not a seat forecast.
- Exclude party, union and advocacy-commissioned polls from the average by default; rare documented exceptions require eligibility_exception.
- Rolling window, one poll per pollster, sample-size and time decay weights.
- Uncertainty bands combine sampling variance and between-poll dispersion.

## Definitions used throughout

- `announced` — a person or media report states an intention to stand; party endorsement is not confirmed
- `endorsed` — a party has preselected or endorsed the person for that seat
- `nominated` — a nomination has been accepted by the electoral commission
- `withdrawn` — the candidacy ended
- `disendorsed` — the party revoked its endorsement
- `elected` / `defeated` — declared by the electoral commission

Rumour and speculation are not recorded at all.
